A. Because the Ld. Trial Court failed to conduct any preliminary enquiry after passing of the order dated 05.02.2022 in Revision Petition as there is no mention of any preliminary enquiry in the impugned order dated 03.07.2024, after disposal of the Revision Petition.

C. Because the Ld. Trial Court failed to appreciate that Ricky Arora, Pradeep Basoya, Abdullah and other unknown members of Crime Syndicate) were first time added in the Complaint U/s 200 Cr P.C. Whereas, the complaint dt. 18.09.2020 was originally filed against Revisionist and the other members namely Nadir Shah, ASI Jai, Ct. Vikas, Babneet, only. This clearly shows the after-thought of the Respondent No 2 to implicate a false case against the Revisionist. 
D. Because the Complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C. is full of improvements over the police complaint dated 18.09.2020 and the complaint made to Vigilance dated 23.09.2020. In the Police Complaints, it has been falsely projected as if Revisionist met the Respondent No 2 for the first time in May 2020,
whereas in the Complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C., the Respondent No 2 claims to know Revisionist much before May 2020. Moreover, Para 1 of the Police Complaint LOVLEEN dated 18.09.2020 contains allegations pertaining to the month of May, 2020. However, no date and time have by LOVLEEN Crl. Also, no criminal complaint was filed in the month of May, 2020.

F. Because in Para 4 of the Police Complaint, allegations have been made to the effect that on 30.07.2020, the Respondent No 2 was forcefully picked up from Jaipur by Revisionist and some policemen. It was alleged that he was beaten throughout the journey to Delhi and was wrongfully confined for four days in East of Kailash, where again he was beaten up and kept without food and water. That the allegations are patently false especially since no police complaint was filed immediately after the alleged incident and there is not even an iota of medical evidence/ MLC/
Medical Reports/ Hospitalization Summary/ Bill or Photographs have been annexed to even prime facie prove the allegations. In addition to that, the Respondent No 2 suggested his wife to return to Delhi separately next morning as the Respondent No 2 feared for the life of his wife. Next day, the Respondent No 2 used his phone to regularly call up his wife. The Respondent No 2 and the Revisionist even stopped by a Dhaba at Delhi- Jaipur Highway to eat dinner which is in sharp contrast to the false version of the allegations of the Respondent No 2.

H. Because it is noteworthy to mention that on the morning of 31.07.2020, the Respondent No 2 himself went out to get breakfast and roam around freely on his own accord, and was in contact with his wife and mother, along with other persons through his own phone, and the same may be verified from his location record and CDRs of his mobile number. It is pertinent to mention that this is completely contrary to the version of the Respondent No 2 that he had been wrongfully detained by Revisionist for 4 days wherein his phone was switched off and he was brutally beaten up.

While in the Police Complaint dated 18.09.2020 and complaint dated 23.09.2020 to the Vigilance, the allegation is that Rs. 5,00,000/- was paid in one shot, whereas in the Complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C, it is alleged that Rs. 5,00,000/- was paid over two days.

It is submitted that even after several requests made by Nadir Shah for the repayment of the loan amounts extended to Respondent No 2 kept falsely assuring him that the loan amount is in safe hands and that the bookie business is reaping big returns and that the Respondent No 2 would return the loan amount soon. That because of the dispute regarding the repayment of loan, the Respondent No. 2 cooked up the stories and levelled false and frivolous allegations against Mr. Nadir Shah and others including the Revisionist. 
S. Because Respondent No 2 grossly failed to make PCR CALL since May, 2020 (first alleged incident) till 18.09.2020. This is evident, that the Respondent No 2 had ample time to approach the police officials to take action against the Revisionist if the alleged allegations had any foundations. 
Meanwhile, the Respondent No 2 moved before the Delhi High Court and filed a Writ seeking inter alia Police protection. 
T. Because the Respondent No 2 failed to join the enquiry. whereas the Revisionist has been duly cooperating with the investigation and abiding by the Digitally Court procedures.

That this not only casts serious doubts on all the allegations leveled by the Respondent No 2 against the Revisionist but also creates great suspicion of the documents filed by the Respondent No 2, before the Hon'ble Court swearing the same by the supporting Affidavit are nothing but merely a move to mislead the Hon'ble Court. 
V. That the Respondent No 2 has filed a wrong and contradictory Affidavit and has played fraud upon this Court without any fear of the Judicial System. The Respondent No 2 has used the forged Inspector Rajinder Singh vs State on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24219712/

Because from a bare perusal of the above said facts, it is amply clear that the Respondent No 2 has himself mislead the court by stating incorrect facts as the same are being contradicted by the Respondent No 2 himself in the police complaint dated 18.09.2020, complaint dated 23.09.2020 annexed with the Complaint U/s 200 Cr.P.C., and also by dishonestly concealing material facts before this Hon'ble Court. Trial Court failed to comply the order dated 05.02.2022 passed by the Revisional court wherein the Revisonal Court said in Para 19 of the order that ".......that registration of an FIR against any person entails serious consequences and the consequences become even graver when the allegations are against any public servant as is the case herein, Respondent No.3,5 and 5 being officials of Delhi Police. Therefore, a preliminary enquiry in a case of such nature, assumes a lot of importance as it may assist the concerned Magistrate to arrive at a just decision." 
4. It is prayed that the impugned order may be set aside. 
5. The prayer of revisionist has been opposed tooth and nail by the respondent. It is submitted that the impugned order is perfectly legal and justified in the facts and circumstances of this case. It is further submitted that the Vigilance Inquiry conducted by the police corroborates the allegations levelled by the respondent and is indicative of the unholy nexus of the revisionist with organized criminal gangs. It is further submitted that the respondent is not seeking arrest of the revisionist,
rather he seeks a fair investigation. It is further submitted that the respondent has not concocted any allegations and that respondent may be proceeded against u/s 182 IPC if the allegations levelled against the revisionist are found incorrect. As such, his allegations may not be dismissed lightly. Ld counsel for Digitally R2 has also filed written submissions. 
signed by LOVLEEN LOVLEEN Date:

State page no. 12 of 16 DISCUSSION 6. This court has considered the rival contentions. Records have also been considered. 
7. The entire law regarding exercise of jurisdiction U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. by a Magistrate has been elaborated recently by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Alok Kumar Vs. Harsh Mander 2023 SSC Online Del 4219. At Para 40, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has observed as under:
Inspector Rajinder Singh vs State on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24219712/
7 "To summarise, a conspectus of the above-mentioned judicial precedents reveal the following :
(i). Power under Section 156(3) Cr. PC necessitates application of judicial mind.
(ii) Such power is to be exercised in a judicious manner, and cannot be exercised mechanically or arbitrarily. 
(iii) Magistrates cannot direct registration of FIR on mere asking of complainant." 
8. It is apparent from the above that a Magistrate has to apply his judicial mind while disposing of a prayer U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. and that directions for registration of an FIR could not be passed in an arbitrary or mechanical manner. 
9. It would be appropriate to reproduce the operative portion of the impugned order for a better understanding of the matter. The Digitally signed by LOVLEEN LOVLEEN Date:
2024.12.04 14:33:17 Crl. Revision No:341/2024 Inspector Rajinder Singh vs. State page no. 13 of 16 +0530 relevant extracts are as under:-
"8. This court has considered the preliminary inquiry as well as the report of the Vigilance Department along with the remaining record and submissions on behalf of the applicant. 
9. On perusal of the entire material, this court finds that the allegations made in the application prima facie reveal commission of cognizable offences of such nature that police investigation is imperative. The allegations include kidnapping for ransom at gunpoint, extortion, beating, criminal intimidation which are cognizable offences. 
The Vigilance inquiry led to directions for creating historysheet for proposed accused no. 1 and transfer of proposed accused no.2, 3 and 4 to non- sensitive postings. 
Though there was a delay in filing complaint with the police, the nature of allegations is grave and requires detailed investigation. It is also noteworthy that the area of Sapna Cinema falls within the jurisdiction of PS Amar Colony and this court and the applicant was brought to an office near Sapna Cinema after being abducted from Jaipur, therefore, part of the alleged offence has taken place wihtin the jurisdiction of PS Amar Colony. 
10. Keeping in mind the totality of the facts and the circumstances, this Court is inclined to invoke the discretionary power vested in the court by virtue of section 156(3) Cr.P.C. as allegations regarding certain cognizable offences have been raised. 
Accordingly the SHO, PS Amar Colony is directed to register an FIR in this case under appropriate sections and submit a LOVLEEN compliance report in this regard. 
It is further directed that the investigation shall not be restricted to the Digitally signed offences alleged in the complaint. It is further made by LOVLEEN Date:
Inspector Rajinder Singh vs State on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24219712/
8 2024.12.04 clear that the power to arrest is different from the need to 14:33:20 +0530 Crl. Revision No:341/2024 Inspector Rajinder Singh vs. State page no. 14 of 16 arrest the accused persons. 
11. Keeping in view that some allegations have been levelled against police officials as well, this Court finds it appropriate to direct the DCP (South East) to supervise/
monitor the investigation of the present case"
10. It is observed by this Court that the relevant factual matrix was duly recorded and considered by the Ld. Magistrate in the impugned order. ATR filed by the police as well as the report of Vigilance Department were also considered by the Ld. Magistrate. Having gone through the TCR, this Court must observe that the allegations levelled by the respondent are very grave and serious in nature. 
The kind of evidence required to be collected in this case seems to be beyond the capability of any public person. Recoveries might also need to be effected promptly. The objections raised by the revisionist in the present proceedings are not sufficient to hold that the allegations levelled by the respondent are completely false and fabricated. Infact, a formal investigation would rather substantiate as to whether or not the infirmities pointed out by the revisionist bear any merits. In the entire facts and circumstances, this court does not find any reason to differ from the opinion of Ld. Magistrate. The order passed by Ld. Magistrate does not seem to be arbitrary, perverse or irrational nor does it reflect any jurisdictional error which occasioned any injustice in the matter. 
The present petition is devoid of any merits and is LOVLEEN hereby dismissed. TCR be sent back alongwith a copy of this 2024.12.04 Crl. Revision No:341/2024 Inspector Rajinder Singh vs. State page no. 15 of 16 LOVLEEN 11. This revision file be consigned to Record Room, as per rules.
